title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: means of salvation offered to reprobates are neither effects of predestination nor media of reprobation — they flow from philanthropy and more general providence; Thomas and Vasquez on the distinction
pass_a_gloss: The means of salvation therefore which are offered unto the reprobate are not effects of predestination; because so they would obtain the end: neither do they flow from the decree of reprobation, as media subordinated by God unto procuring the damnation of the reprobate; because it belongs not unto God to provide of means leading the reprobate unto everlasting death, which abound from themselves if God oppose not special grace; but they flow from that philanthropy and more general providence, which so disposes means unto some end, that meanwhile it permits the second cause by its own fault to fall short of obtaining the end. This discrimination between Predestination and Providence Thomas well explained, Quaest. Disp. De praed. art. 1. And Vasquez himself acknowledges the same, In 1. quaest. 22. disp. 87. cap. 4. at the very end of the chapter.
pass_b_english: So the means of salvation offered to the reprobate are not effects of predestination — else they would reach the end. Nor do they flow from the reprobation decree as media God subordinated to procuring their damnation — for it is not God's part to furnish means that lead reprobates to everlasting death; those sprout abundantly from themselves if he does not oppose special grace. They flow instead from that philanthropy and more general providence which so disposes means toward an end that it meanwhile permits the second cause, by its own fault, to fall short of attaining it. Thomas well explains this distinction between Predestination and Providence (Quaest. Disp. De praed. art. 1); Vasquez acknowledges the same (In 1 q.22 disp. 87 c.4, at the chapter's end).
source_text: Media igitur salutis quae offeruntur reprobatis non sunt effectus praedestinationis; quia sic finem consequerentur: neque fluunt a decreto reprobationis, tanquam media ad procurandam reprobatorum damnationem a Deo subordinata; quia non pertinet ad Deum providere de mediis reprobatos ad mortem aeternam ducentibus, quae ex ipsis abunde pullulant, si Deus gratiam specialem non opponat; sed manant ab illa φιλανθρωπίᾳ et generaliore providentia, quae media ad aliquem finem ita disponit, ut interim permittat causam secundam a consecutione finis suo vitio excidere. Hoc discrimen inter Praedestinationem et Providentiam bene explicavit Thomas, Quaest. Disp. De praed. art. 1. Eamque agnoscit ipse Vasques, In 1. quaest. 22. disp. 87. cap. 4. in ipso fine capitis.
